title: Organ
description: Metaphor→Mechanism W6.4 (design-register: declared-organs). A typed, queryable view of a functional group of services in the mesh — the organogenesis design's first mechanical form. v1 is DECLARED, not emergent: organs are asserted over services that already exist (memory, routing, perception, policy) and report live member health, so the mesh's capabilities become inspectable instead of implicit. INVARIANT OR-I1: an organ NEVER invents members — every member corresponds to a real, addressable service, and a member whose health cannot be determined is reported `unknown`, never assumed healthy. INVARIANT OR-I2: organ health is derived from members, never asserted independently — an organ cannot claim to be healthier than the members it is made of. Membership dynamics (v2) and differentiation (v3) are deliberately out of scope until v1 proves useful.

kind.description: The function this organ performs for the whole: memory retains, routing directs, perception ingests/extracts, policy governs.

members.description: Real services composing the organ (OR-I1). Never synthetic.

health.description: `unknown` when health could not be determined — never optimistically 'healthy' (OR-I1).

capabilities.description: What this organ can do, as capability tokens the membrane/registry already speaks.

health.description: Derived from members only (OR-I2): healthy iff all known members are healthy; down iff all are down; unknown iff no member health is known; degraded otherwise.
